problem: It says 'A match in the MPCP instance corresponds to a halting computation of M on w.' A computation that halts but rejects does not give a match. The closing dominoes of the encoding can only be applied when the machine is in the accepting state, so the correspondence is with an accepting computation, not with any halting one. The chapter's own opening line of Section 3 (the acceptance problem) contradicts this sentence.
fix: Say: 'A match in the MPCP instance corresponds to an accepting computation of M on w, that is, one that halts in the accept state. If M halts without accepting, or never halts, the instance has no match.'
